subjects.label: Accounting
subjects.summary: Ledger, statements, ratios and the cost-volume-profit questions built on them.
start_steps: Check what you already have: a journal and a trial balance go to Check a trial balance; a blank set of books goes to Management accounts.
Build or read the statements: period, currency, chart of accounts, opening balances and entries; then confirm the account mapping.
Read the statements with Financial statement ratios and Common-size and trend.
For a cost question, use Cost-volume-profit, Activity-based costing or Sales variances.
does_not: It does not file a tax return or apply a jurisdiction's tax law; tax is a declared-rate calculation.
It does not choose the accounting policy, audit the figures or certify the statements.
It does not invent a missing balance or plug an unbalanced trial balance.

subjects.label: Finance
subjects.summary: Corporate finance, valuation and the investments, debt, risk and international tools a finance student needs.
start_steps: One cash flow or instrument: Time value of money, Loan amortization or Bond price and duration.
A project: NPV, IRR and Discounted payback, then Project ranking metrics and Scenario analysis.
A company: WACC, DCF valuation, the Equity bridge and Comparable multiples.
An investment or risk question: CAPM, Portfolio return and risk, Value at risk and Option pricing.
An international question: FX and interest parity, then Currency conversion.
does_not: It does not retrieve market prices, yields, exchange rates or peer multiples; you declare them.
It does not choose the discount rate, the peer set or the risk appetite for you.
It does not model tax, American exercise, liquidity risk or a full portfolio optimisation.

subjects.label: Economics
subjects.summary: The quantitative economics core: micro, macro, welfare, international, development, behavioural, game theory and impact evaluation.
start_steps: A market question: Market equilibrium, then Elasticity, Tax incidence or Price ceilings and floors.
A national or policy question: GDP and national income, Inflation and real interest, Unemployment and participation, then the money or fiscal multiplier.
A welfare or inequality question: Externalities and Pigouvian tax, Public goods, Social welfare, Gini coefficient and Poverty measures.
An international question: Comparative advantage, Tariff welfare, Purchasing-power parity and Interest-rate parity.
An evidence question: use the Advanced econometrics tools only when the data and design are declared.
does_not: It does not retrieve GDP, CPI, market or household data; you declare every input.
It does not estimate a demand curve, a model or a causal effect from raw data.
It does not make a policy recommendation or prove that one policy is better.

subjects.label: Management & strategy
subjects.summary: Structure the evidence on a competitive position, then compare the options that follow.
start_steps: Choose the worksheet that matches the question: Five Forces, PESTEL, SWOT, Value Chain or a canvas.
Write the evidence you have, one item per line, and label it as your evidence, sourced or an assumption.
Read the gaps and the evidence audit: what is missing stays missing.
Compare the options with the decision tools or the weighted matrix.
does_not: It does not generate evidence or fill a blank quadrant or cell.
It does not score or rank the frameworks.
It does not choose the strategy for you.

subjects.label: Project management
subjects.summary: Govern a project, record the documents that deliver it, appraise its business case, compare the options, and plan and control the schedule.
start_steps: Govern the project: a balanced scorecard, a strategy map, a KPI tree and a set of OKRs.
Write the project charter: what the project is for, what is in and out of scope, and who authorises it.
Appraise the business case: NPV, IRR, payback and the option to invest or delay.
Compare the options: scenario analysis, a decision tree or the weighted decision matrix.
Plan the schedule: critical path, resources, crashing, calendars and shared projects.
Control delivery: earned value, schedule risk and the Monte Carlo range.
Record the delivery documents: WBS, RACI, risk register, stakeholder plan and lessons learned.
does_not: It does not invent durations, probabilities, weights, owners or terminal values; you declare them.
It does not choose the project or the option for you beyond the declared rule.
It does not level resources optimally, level across calendars or simulate correlated risks.
It does not score, weight or rank your objectives, measures or risks; an empty cell is named, never filled.

subjects.label: Entrepreneurship
subjects.summary: Test a venture idea: market size, price, break-even, cash and the capital it needs.
start_steps: Start with the business plan: market size, price and break-even.
Plan the cash and capital: start-up capital, cash runway and loan.
Appraise the return: NPV, IRR, payback and the scenario range.
Test the venture model with Unit economics and the canvas worksheets.
does_not: It does not invent a market size, price, cost or growth rate.
It does not raise the capital, validate the idea or guarantee a return.
It does not replace a customer interview or a real market test.

subjects.label: Operations management
subjects.summary: Cost-volume-profit, process evidence and the statistics used to inspect a process.
start_steps: Cost and volume: Break-even point or Multi-product break-even.
Capacity and flow: Capacity and utilisation, Queueing, or Line balancing.
Inventory: Inventory and EOQ, with the Trend forecast for demand.
Quality: OEE or Statistical process control; use the statistics tools to test a process change.
does_not: It does not retrieve production, time or quality data; you declare it.
It does not optimise a full schedule, a shift plan or a stochastic process.
It does not replace a plant visit or a direct process observation.

subjects.label: Supply chain & logistics
subjects.summary: The same evidence tools as Operations, with the inventory and network gaps stated plainly.
start_steps: Inventory: Inventory and EOQ, with the Trend forecast for demand.
Capacity and service: Capacity and utilisation, or Queueing.
Cost of a supply option: Break-even point and Unit economics.
Incomplete data: Missing-data bounds, so the gap is named rather than guessed.
does_not: It does not design a network, optimise routing or select a supplier.
It does not retrieve freight, tariff or supplier data.
It does not model disruption, multi-echelon inventory or a full logistics simulation.

subjects.label: Marketing & customers
subjects.summary: Plan the marketing and then measure it: market size and demand, customer economics, campaign and channel performance, and the surveys and tests behind customer evidence.
start_steps: Size the market: Market size and Market share.
Check demand: Demand curve, Elasticity and Purchase intent.
Test customer economics: Unit economics, Cohort, RFM and CLV.
Measure the funnel and channels: Funnel, Campaign, Attribution, Channel economics and the channel tools.
Test a change: A/B test, Reliability (alpha), Chi-square and Power.
does_not: It does not connect to an ad platform or retrieve campaign data.
It does not recommend a budget, a bid or a segment.
It does not estimate a missing number or invent a customer.

subjects.label: People & organisation
subjects.summary: Design the job, develop the people who do it, and read the organisation they work in.
start_steps: Name the decision you are taking: the job, the training, the team, the change or the design.
Open the tile that holds it and read what the framework needs before you start.
Write the brief: what you know, what you have observed and what you want the paper to settle.
Check the evidence on every part and add your own where the pipeline found nothing.
Read the limitations before you cite it: each framework here states what it cannot settle.
does_not: The reward tile is empty because no reward or job-evaluation framework is in the catalogue.

It does not compute headcount, turnover, absence, cost per hire, time to hire, compa-ratio, span of control, diversity, engagement or a nine-box score: the frozen core has no such method, and a similar method is not a substitute for it.
The frameworks here record and evidence a decision; they do not design the role, run the training, choose the intervention or predict who will succeed.
A catalogue-only framework is something to read and cite. It is not a worksheet until the owner builds one.

subjects.label: Research & statistics
subjects.summary: The cross-cutting method shelf: every statistical method the engine can run, linked from every subject.
start_steps: Describe the data: Descriptive statistics.
Compare groups: Welch two-sample t-test, Mann-Whitney U, One-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis.
Relate variables: Pearson or Spearman correlation, Linear regression or Logistic regression.
Check the design: Power and sample size, Multiple-comparison correction and Missing-data bounds.
does_not: It does not design the study, choose the hypothesis or clean the data for you.
It does not prove causality from observational data.
It does not replace a statistician for a complex or clustered design.
